note: Phase 14: kg's reader gains Emacs' symbol escapes. A backslash takes the next byte into the name literally, one escape anywhere makes the token a symbol rather than a number, and an escaped dot is an ordinary list element where a bare one is the dotted-tail marker -- so `(a \. b)` has three elements and `(a\ b)` has one. Measured before the pin move: E:unsupported read syntax: symbol escape.
